QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_3

question.text: The outstanding stock of a Government bond is Rs. 80,000 crores. Per the workbook's exchange-level cap, what is the maximum permissible overall open position across all IRD contracts on this underlying?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 235 of the NISM Series IV workbook, the exchange-level overall open position limit across all IRD contracts on a specific underlying bond shall not exceed 25% of the outstanding underlying bond. 25% of Rs. 80,000 crore = Rs. 20,000 crore. The Trap: Rs. 12,000 crore uses 15%, which is not the source-backed exchange-level overall cap. Rs. 8,000 crore uses 10%; Rs. 16,000 crore uses 20%. The workbook prescribes the 25% rule for the exchange-level overall IRD open position on a specific underlying bond. Note: Per pages 234-235 and 237 of Series IV, separate open-interest-based limits apply at member/client level for GOI bond futures; the 25%-of-outstanding cap applies at the exchange-level overall IRD position on a single underlying.
